criteria.name: Introduction: mission concept and rationale. Include the following required information: What is the spacecraft's primary mission? Why is the mission needed? How many spacecraft are used and why? Who are the users (operator and customers)?
criteria.reasoning: All four required questions are answered with justification: mission need is built from the limits of existing bleaching monitoring, single-satellite choice is argued, and operator and customers are named. References [1]-[6] support the rationale. Minor gaps: some claims are uncited (reliance of humans on reefs, government funding), and the tone is informal in places.

evidence.quote: The primary mission of ZYZZsat is to image the whole Great Barrier Reef in visible bands at 5 m resolution
The operator is the Australian Institute of Marine Science (AIMS), which already runs the long-term monitoring program for the reef

criteria.name: Main body: mission design. Present a summary of the mission design using software and/or hand calculations as appropriate. Include relevant screenshots and software files in the main body of the report and/or appendix. Include the following information: Where will it launch from, and using which launch vehicle? Why did you choose this option? What type of orbit will you use? What are its characteristics and orbital elements? Will you need to perform any orbital maneuvers? Which ground control facilities will you use? How often will your spacecraft be able to communicate with ground control? How long will the mission last, and what are your plans for EOL?
criteria.reasoning: Strong, largely verified calculations: launch azimuth, J2 inclination, 771 s maximum pass, access statistics, drag decay and data budget all check out. Accuracy is reduced by errors and inconsistencies: 510 s of 771 s is about 66 percent, not 60; the 34-minute eclipse looks high for an 08:45 node; the 60,000 km² daily area conflicts with the 45-day mosaic; the link budget is unclosed.

criteria.name: Report presentation
criteria.reasoning: Clear report structure with executive summary, numbered sections, numbered and captioned tables and figures, and consistent IEEE-style references. Weaknesses: informal phrasing in places, some uncited claims, and a downlink margin given as about three times in the summary but 3.5 in Section 2.4.

technical_issues.issue: 510 s of 771 s is about 66 percent of a pass, not 60 percent. Using 66 percent gives about 38 min/day, changing the 34-min figure and the downlink margin.
A 34-minute eclipse implies a beta angle near 10 degrees. An 08:45 node time gives roughly 28 min by estimate (beta about 49 degrees). Verify in STK or correct the figure.

One 60 km x 1,000 km strip per day gives about 6 days to image the 344,400 km2 reef, conflicting with the 45-day nadir mosaic and the reef-coverage narrative. The daily imaging assumption is not reconciled with track geometry.

Lifetime is estimated as scale height divided by a constant decay rate using one density, which is crude. Decay rates change strongly with altitude, so the 32-year and 2.2-year figures need numerical propagation or a caveat.
The 50 Mbit/s X-band downlink margin is presented as adequate without a link budget. This is acknowledged but weakens the conclusion.
The facility file extension is given as .f; STK facility files normally use .fac. Check that the submitted files open in STK.

overall: Comprehensive, mostly accurate mission design with verified orbit, launch and drag calculations and strong structure. Deductions for numerical inconsistencies (contact fraction, eclipse time, revisit versus daily area), an unclosed link budget, some uncited claims and informal phrasing.

feedback.summary: You have produced a strong, well-structured mission design for ZYZZsat. Your introduction answers the required questions clearly, and your orbit, launch and drag work is well supported by STK and hand calculations. Your conclusions are specific and tied to the evidence. The main improvements are numerical consistency: the contact-time fraction, the eclipse duration, the daily imaging area against the 45-day mosaic, and the unclosed X-band link budget. Some claims also need citations and a more formal tone.
next_steps: Correct the contact-time fraction (510 s of 771 s is about 66 percent, not 60 percent) and recalculate the daily contact time and downlink margin in Section 2.4 and the Executive Summary.
Verify the eclipse duration in STK or correct the beta-angle statement, and reconcile the daily imaging area in Table 6 with the 45-day mosaic in Table 3.
Close the X-band link budget, check the 32-year lifetime with numerical propagation, cite the uncited claims, and confirm that the Appendix A facility files open in STK.

criteria.C1: You answer all four required questions clearly. The mission need is built from the limits of current bleaching monitoring, you justify using a single satellite, and you name AIMS as operator and identify the customers. References [1]-[6] support the rationale. To strengthen it further, cite the claims about human reliance on reefs and government funding, and use a more formal tone in places.
criteria.C2: Your launch azimuth, J2 inclination, pass statistics, drag decay and data budget are largely verified and well supported by STK. Some key figures need correcting. 510 s of a 771 s pass is about 66 percent, not 60 percent, which changes the daily contact time and downlink margin. The 34-minute eclipse does not fit an 08:45 node, and the daily imaging area in Table 6 conflicts with the 45-day mosaic. Close the X-band link budget to support the downlink conclusion.
criteria.C3: Your conclusions are specific and tied to the evidence, restating revisit times, pass statistics, downlink margin and decay lifetime with numbers. Identifying four limitations with their consequences and next steps is a clear strength. To make the conclusion fully robust, ensure the figures it restates match the corrected values in Sections 2.3 and 2.4, and cite the claim that reef managers prefer weekly coverage.
criteria.C4: Your report has a clear structure, an executive summary, numbered and captioned tables and figures, and consistent IEEE-style references. To improve polish, remove informal phrasing and make the downlink margin consistent between the Executive Summary (about three times) and Section 2.4 (3.5). Also check the facility file extension in Table A1, since STK normally uses .fac.
